other_conditions: Child must meet at least one of the listed vulnerability conditions (family breakdown, crisis, safety at risk, disaster, orphaned/abandoned, not eligible for adoption, institutionalised child needing reinstatement, or in conflict with law)
Foster parents must have stable emotional adjustment and be physically, mentally, and emotionally stable
Foster parents must have sufficient income to meet the basic needs of the child
Medical fitness of all family members must be verified (including HIV, TB, Hepatitis B tests)
Foster parents must have adequate exposure, orientation and capacity in child caring
The home should have adequate space and basic facilities
Foster family must agree to regular paediatrician visits, immunizations and maintain the child's health records
Foster family must sign an agreement and return the child to the Child Welfare Committee if directed
Foster parents must attend training or orientation programmes on child care and health
Foster parents must motivate the child to study and ensure schooling or vocational training
No discrimination on the basis of caste, religion, ethnic status, disability or health status
Not more than two children may be placed in a foster family unless they are siblings
benefits_summary: Foster families receive a monthly allowance of ₹2,500, plus a maintenance allowance based on the child’s age (₹1,500 for 0‑6 years, ₹2,000 for 6‑14 years, ₹2,500 for 14‑18 years).
documents_required: Medical reports of all family members (including HIV, TB, Hepatitis B tests)
